HISTORY
For 125 years, Royal Enﬁeld has been guided by a simple yet 
enduring belief: that motorcycling is not just about going from 
A to B, it’s about how the ride makes you feel. This conviction 
has shaped every machine we’ve built, every community we’ve 
nurtured and every journey we’ve enabled across 
generations of riders. 

Reaching this milestone tells the story of a company that has 
continuously evolved with the times while staying rooted in 
its core philosophy. From humble beginnings — one machine, 
one market, one idea — we have grown into a global force. Today, 
we are present in more than 80 countries, with a portfolio that 
spans roadsters, cruisers, adventure tourers and now, electric 
motorcycles. From one motorcycle to many. From India to the 
world. This is more than just growth; it is a transformation 
achieved without ever losing sight of who we are. 
Our geography alone tells a remarkable story. What began in 
Britain and found its home in India has since travelled across 
continents — taking root in the mountain communities of the 
Himalayas, the coastal highways of Latin America, the city 
streets of Southeast Asia and the open highways of Europe 
and Australia. Today, Royal Enﬁeld is the undisputed leader in 
the global midsize motorcycle segment, not because we 
chased every market, but because we built something 
authentic. Our motorcycles are built with purpose, not just 
precision. Riders in Brazil, Thailand and New Zealand are 
drawn to the same thing that captivated riders 
in Chennai and Chandigarh decades ago. 
GLOBAL 
FOOTPRINT

Our journey is one of quiet, continuous evolution. From the 
legendary Bullet — the longest-running motorcycle in 
continuous production — to the Himalayan, which created a 
new category of accessible adventure; from the 650 Twins, 
which cemented our global leadership, to the Flying Flea, our 
ﬁrst foray into electric mobility. Each generation of 
motorcycles has reﬂected its era while honouring what came 
before. And through it all, our Royal Enﬁeld community has 
always been part of the process, shaping our motorcycles 
through their experiences, feedback and journeys. Royal Enﬁeld 
motorcycles have always been built for riders, by riders.
EVOLUTION

COMMUNITY 
& FUTURE
The relationship between company and our community is the 
foundation of everything we do. It has grown organically over 
125 years and cannot be manufactured or marketed — only 
nurtured. Our community does not just ride our motorcycles; 
it carries the culture forward. It brings the joy of 
Pure Motorcycling to every corner of the earth, ensuring this 
visceral experience ﬁnds everyone who seeks it.
In its 125th year, Royal Enﬁeld continues to deliver consistent 
growth, record revenues and a brand value that ranks among the 
strongest in the global automotive industry. But what no 
balance sheet can capture is the millions of riders across the 
world who do not just own a Royal Enﬁeld, but belong to a global 
community because of it.  
This is the truest measure of our 125 years. Not the numbers, but 
the feeling those numbers represent. This is our legacy. This is 
our foundation. And this is where our next chapter begins.
Pure Motorcycling since 1901.

ABOUT THE REPORT
FY 2025-26 marks Eicher Motors Limited’s (EML) 
fifth year of integrated reporting, reflecting our 
commitment to transparency and long-term 
value creation.
Aligned with the principles of the Integrated 
Reporting <IR> Framework, developed by the 
International Integrated Reporting Council (IIRC) 
and now a part of the International Financial 
Reporting Standards, the Report captures how our 
strategy, governance, performance, and outlook 
shape sustainable growth.
Through such reporting, we provide stakeholders 
with comprehensive insights into how we create, 
protect, and grow value over time. We capture how 
we use the six capitals – Financial, Manufactured, 
Human, Intellectual, Natural, and Social & 
Relationship – in our operations, while considering 
externalities, material topics, emerging risks, and 
stakeholder engagement outcomes. We go beyond 
to provide the strategic way forward to maximise 
value creation. The Report reflects how sustainable 
development remains embedded within our 
strategic thinking and operational decisions, with 
long-term objectives aligned to the United Nations 
Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
REPORTING PRINCIPLE
This Report is prepared in accordance with the 
<IR> Framework, with reference to the Global 
Reporting Initiative (GRI) and in alignment with 
the core principles of the Business Responsibility 
and Sustainability Reporting (BRSR) requirements 
issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of 
India (SEBI). The financial and statutory sections 
of this Report comply with the Companies Act, 
2013, Indian Accounting Standards, SEBI (Listing 
Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015, the Secretarial Standards 
issued by the Institute of Company Secretaries of 
India, and other applicable regulations.
REPORTING PERIOD, SCOPE AND 
BOUNDARY
This Report covers quantitative and qualitative 
disclosures for the period April 1, 2025, to March 31, 
2026. It encompasses EML’s operations, including 
the corporate headquarters in Chennai, its four 
domestic manufacturing facilities at Thiruvottiyur, 
Oragadam, Vallam Vadagal, and Cheyyar, as well 
as the technical centres in Bruntingthorpe, UK, and 
Chennai, India. The integrated report sections does 
not cover EML's joint ventures and subsidiaries.
APPROACH TO MATERIALITY
The Report’s content and structure are guided by 
Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) issues 
that are material to EML and its stakeholders. These 
issues have been identified through a structured, 
multichannel engagement with internal stakeholders, 
followed by prioritisation based on relevance and impact. 
In FY  2023‑24, we undertook a materiality assessment 
exercise to update our understanding of the key matters, 
informed by internal and external inputs. These matters 
remain relevant for FY 2025‑26, and are integrated into our 
long‑term strategic planning to support sustainable growth.
EXTERNAL ASSURANCE
We engaged DNV Business Assurance India Pvt. Ltd (DNV), 
as an independent third party to provide reasonable 
assurance on the core parameters of BRSR presented in 
this Integrated Annual Report. The assurance statement 
can be found on page 223.
RESTATEMENT
Certain restatements have been made in this Report and 
have been appropriately disclosed in the relevant sections, 
as required.
MANAGEMENT RESPONSIBILITY
EML’s management team has reviewed the contents of 
this Report and undertakes responsibility for the integrity 
of the information. They believe, to the best of their 
knowledge, that the Report provides a complete picture of 
the value creation and captures all relevant material issues 
transparently and accurately.
FEEDBACK
We are committed to listening to the feedback and 
viewpoints of all our stakeholders. We welcome your 
comments, enquiries, and recommendations on 
business and sustainability to help us improve our 
performance and its reporting. We invite you to write 
to us with your feedback, questions, and suggestions 
at: investors@eichermotors.com. Further, details of 
EML’s sustainability performance are available on the 
corporate website: www.eichermotors.com
FORWARD-LOOKING STATEMENT
The Report makes use of certain statements related 
to the Company’s business operations, industry, 
objectives, business strategy, management plans, and 
expectations. These forward-looking statements can 
be denoted by usage of words such as ‘anticipates’, 
‘believes’, ‘estimates’, ‘expects’, ‘intends’, ‘may’, 
‘outlook’, ‘plans’, ‘will’ and other similar words that 
imply future operating or financial performance of the 
Company. Since forward-looking statements are reliant 
on assumptions, there is a probability of incorrect 
data or methods with little potential of being fulfilled. 
These statements are intended to establish our current 
expectations according to logical assumptions and not 
act as a guarantee of future outcomes. The Company’s 
actual results could be affected by various factors, 
risks, and uncertainties and could vary materially 
from the projections indicated by the forward-
looking statements. The Company is not under any 
obligation nor has any intention to update or revise any 
forward‑looking statements in case of future events.

ABOUT EICHER MOTORS LIMITED
Eicher Motors Limited (EML) is a global automobile company headquartered in Chennai, India, and 
listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange.
EML is the parent company of Royal Enfield, the global leader in the mid-size motorcycle 
segment (250cc - 750cc) and operates a joint venture with Volvo Group - VE Commercial 
Vehicles Limited (VECV), a pioneer in commercial vehicles.

SHAPING JOURNEYS, FROM PURE 
MOTORCYCLING TO SMART MOBILITY
ROYAL ENFIELD
The oldest motorcycle brand in 
continuous production, Royal Enfield 
has created beautifully crafted 
motorcycles since 1901. From its British 
roots, a manufacturing plant was 
established in Madras (now Chennai) 
in 1955, a foothold from which Royal 
Enfield spearheaded the growth of 
India’s mid-sized two-wheeler segment. 
Royal Enfield Motorcycles are engaging, 
uncomplicated, accessible, and fun 
to ride; a vehicle for exploration and 
self‑expression. It’s an approach 
the brand calls ‘Pure Motorcycling’. 
Complemented by its allied businesses, 
Royal Enfield continues to create a 
holistic ecosystem that strengthens 
its bond with riders. The Company has 
4 manufacturing plants in Tamil Nadu 
and 7 CKD (Completely knocked down) 
assembly units.
The Company recently unveiled its new 
City+ electric mobility brand – the Flying 
Flea – a fresh take on urban mobility, 
blending authentic design with advanced 
technology, developed entirely in-house 
at the Company's tech centres.
VE COMMERCIAL VEHICLES 
LIMITED
VE Commercial Vehicles Limited (VECV) 
is a joint venture between the Volvo 
Group and Eicher Motors Limited. In 
operation since August 2008, the 
company includes the complete 
range of Eicher branded trucks and 
buses, Volvo Buses and exclusive 
distribution of Volvo Trucks in India, 
engine manufacturing and exports for 
Volvo Group, Eicher Power Solutions 
and Eicher Engineering Components. 
A multi-brand, multi-division company, 
backed by innovative products and 
services, VECV today, is recognised 
as an industry leader for modernising 
commercial transportation in India and 
the developing markets.

Dear Shareholders,
Last year, in my first note as Executive 
Chairman, I wrote about three priorities: 
strengthening governance, preparing 
our businesses for their next phase 
of growth, and navigating the biggest 
technology shift our industry has ever 
seen. One year on, the world has not 
become any calmer – geopolitics keeps 
shifting, supply chains keep getting 
tested, and customer expectations 
keep evolving. All the more reason to 
think long, stay responsive, and remain 
focused on what truly matters.
And what a year it has been.
Royal Enfield completed 125 years. 
We crossed ten million cumulative 
motorcycles since inception and sold 
more than 1.2 million in a single year 
– more than we made and sold in our 
entire first century. VE Commercial 
Vehicles crossed 100,000 annual 
vehicle deliveries for the first time. 
Together, these milestones reflect how 
both businesses have been built: with 
discipline, long-term focus and absolute 
clarity about who we serve.
The 125th year gives us a rare chance to 
look back with perspective. When Royal 
Enfield turned 100, we were struggling 
for survival. Twenty-five years later, we 
are the oldest motorcycle manufacturer 
in continuous production – and at our 
all-time peak. That did not happen by 
chasing every trend. It happened by 
staying close to riders, making clear 
choices, and following our own path 
even when it looked unfashionable.
Today, Royal Enfield is the number 
one mid-size motorcycle brand in the 
world. Our motorcycles are ridden from 
Mongolia to the tip of Argentina, and we 
have become one of the few truly global 
premium consumer brands from India.
We are marking the 125th in style, all 
year long. At Redditch, the site of our 
first factory, a World Origin plaque now 
stands where it all began in 1901 – with 
five generations of our motorcycles 
lining Enfield Road for the unveiling. 
We have also launched the Classic 650 
125th Anniversary Special Edition while 
riders and communities around the 
world are coming together through our 
celebratory showcase at EICMA, and 
special editions of Motoverse and One 
Ride, which this year is expected to bring 
together more than 125,000 riders 
across the globe. The anniversary is not 
only a celebration of our history, but of 
the global community that continues to 
carry Royal Enfield forward.
The year also tested us. Restrictions on 
rare-earth magnets emerged in the first 
week of the financial year, disrupting 
supplies across the global automotive 
industry, while commodity prices 
remained a stiff headwind through 
the year. Some of our production was 
affected early on, but our teams moved 
quickly on alternate sources, value 
engineering and calibrated pricing, 
and largely offset the impact. When 
you have been around for 125 years, 
you can afford to think long – and 
act  quickly.
None of this has slowed our build-
out. We are investing C 958 Crores in 
a major expansion of Cheyyar – our 
fourth and newest plant in Tamil Nadu 
– which will take Royal Enfield’s total 
annual installed capacity to two million 
motorcycles. Our proposed greenfield 
facility in Andhra Pradesh will create 
further capacity for Royal Enfield’s next 
decade of global growth.
And now, for the first time since 1955 – 
when India became our home – we are 
adding a new home market: Brazil. It is 
already our second-largest market, and 
we are committing to go deep: in our 
brand, our teams, local manufacturing 
and our network. To enable our growth, 
we have doubled our dealership network

FY 2025-26 was also Royal Enfield’s 
strongest year yet. We crossed 
1.2  Million motorcycles in annual 
sales, our highest ever, with domestic 
volumes growing 23% to 11,07,343  units 
and international sales rising 20% to 
1,20,634 units. The festive season in 
Q3 was the strongest in our history,

for the rider who wants more without 
wanting it to be something different. The 
2025 Hunter 350 continued this story 
with updates that were immediately 
embraced by riders, cementing its place 
as the definitive urban motorcycle 
in its class. The 2025 Meteor 350, 
the 2026 Goan Classic 350, and the 
Himalayan 450 each received their 
own updates – evolving with purpose, 
while staying true to character. Several 
products in the portfolio also achieved 
key milestones in their journeys. The 
Meteor 350 crossed six Lakh units in 
cumulative sales since launch and the 
Himalayan 450 had its strongest year 
to date, crossing 38,000 global sales 
while recording over 53% growth in 
international markets.
One of the most significant steps we 
took this year was the launch of our first 
electric motorcycle – the Flying Flea 
C6 – in April 2026, and the opening of 
our first Flying Flea store in Bengaluru. 
Flying Flea is our vision for City+ electric 
mobility and our approach to building 
this category is very clear. We will do 
it steadily, with a long-term intent, 
focussing on design that is functional 
and full of character, technology that 
serves the rider, and an ownership 
experience that goes beyond the 
machine. The response to the FF.C6 has 
been extremely encouraging.
Beyond India, we continued to deepen 
our global footprint. The LATAM region 
registered 20% overall growth, led by 
a strong 71% growth in Brazil, which is 
now our largest and fastest-growing 
international market, a testament to 
how far the spirit of Pure Motorcycling 
has travelled and how genuinely 
it has taken root in cultures and 
communities far beyond where we 
began. Across Europe and Asia, we 
continued to strengthen our presence 
in the mid‑size motorcycling segment.

mid-size segment in Europe, while also 
holding strong positions across key 
markets such as the UK, Italy, France, 
and Germany. In Asia too, we have 
established ourselves as the #2 player 
in markets including Thailand, Korea, 
and New Zealand. Closer to home, 
we are #1 in the mid-size segment 
across the SAARC region. This is a 
disciplined expansion that reflects 
the increasing global relevance of the 
Royal  Enfield  brand.
To support this growing demand, we 
recently announced a C 958 Crores 
investment towards a brownfield 
expansion of our Cheyyar facility in 
Tamil Nadu. This phased expansion, 
expected to be completed by

production capacity to 2 million units. 
This strategic investment reflects 
our confidence in the strength of our 
product pipeline and the long-term 
opportunity ahead of us. We have 
consciously chosen the brownfield route 
as an efficient way to leverage existing 
infrastructure, optimising capital 
deployment, and ensuring operational 
continuity. Most importantly, it ensures 
that we remain future-ready as our 
global community of riders continues 
to grow.

Flying Flea
Flying Flea is not just about going electric – it is about 
creating a new category. It reflects a clear intent to build 
products that are deeply connected to the city and the 
rider, where agility, technology and experience come 
together in a way that is intuitive, purposeful, and distinct. 
Powered by a team of 200+ engineers across India and the 
UK, and backed by 45+ patent applications, Flying Flea is 
developed entirely in-house.

With the launch of the FF.C6 in April 
2026, Flying Flea embarked on its 
journey as Royal Enfield’s new City+ 
electric mobility brand. The first product 
under the brand, the FF.C6 has been 
thoughtfully reinterpreted for today’s 
urban rider, blending authentic design, 
lightweight agility, and advanced 
connected technology to deliver a 
deeply intuitive riding experience.
A homage to the original Flying Flea 
of the 1940s, engineered for frontline 
troops, the FF.C6 reinterprets the 
spirit of lightness and adaptability for 
today’s rider. Hardcoded to be agile, 
visceral, and resilient, it delivers a 
deeply intuitive riding experience where 
hardware and software seamlessly work 
as one, engineered to connect, adapt, 
and evolve with its rider.
The FF.C6 is an embodiment of Artistry, 
Wizardry, and Chemistry. Artistry comes 
alive in the precision-engineered forged 
aluminium Girder fork, a contemporary 
interpretation of the original Flying 
Flea’s iconic front suspension. The 
battery fins further reflect the Flying 
Flea ethos, bringing together tradition 
and innovation through a distinctive 
wing-shaped design inspired by 
motion and balance. Wizardry is 
reflected in a system that continuously 
learns from rider behaviour, with 
over-the-air updates and seamless 
control. Chemistry is delivered through 
a 3.91 kWh lithium-ion battery, 
best-in-class regenerative braking, 
instant acceleration, and advanced 
stability systems for a ride that is 
efficient, predictable, and effortlessly 
adaptable to the rider’s world.
Through the year, the motorcycle 
was showcased globally across major 
cities, building momentum ahead of 
its official India launch alongside the 
opening of the first Flying Flea store 
in Bengaluru, India. The FF.C6 also 
emerged as a significant global design 
statement, winning the Red Dot Design 
Award 2025 in the Design Concept 
category, the 2025 Good Design Award 
in the Transportation category, and 
the iF Design Award 2026 in Product 
Design and Automotive category. These 
recognitions reinforce the motorcycle’s 
compelling neo-vintage interpretation 
of electric mobility, blending emotion, 
craftsmanship, and contemporary 
urban functionality.
FF.C6: The First Expression of Flying Flea
SEXY SCIENCE

moving forever forward, Flying Flea 
unveiled the scrambler-styled FF.S6, 
a City+ explorer engineered for agility, 
adaptability, and adventure, at EICMA 
2025. The new FF.S6 builds on the 
same ethos and platform as the FF.C6, 
carrying forward a DNA rooted in

high-torque motor and long suspension 
travel, paired with an enduro-style seat

addition to the Flying Flea portfolio.
The FF.S6 was showcased at Motoverse in

a lightweight electric scrambler aimed at

roads and mild trails on the weekend. The

a working template for how the brand 
wants its first generation of electric 
motorcycles to feel and function.

ONE COMMUNITY, COUNTLESS ROADS
21ST EDITION OF HIMALAYAN ODYSSEY
Royal Enfield flagged off the 21st edition of the Himalayan Odyssey, marking over two 
decades of its iconic motorcycling expedition. Spanning 18 days and over 2,600 kms, 
the ride brought together 77 riders from across the globe, traversing the breathtaking 
terrains of Ladakh, Spiti, and Zanskar, including Umling La – the world’s highest 
motorable pass. Divided into two routes, Team Spiti and Team Zanskar, the journey 
combined physical endurance with cultural immersion, beginning with a traditional 
Ladakhi blessing ceremony. Reinforcing its commitment to responsible travel, the 
expedition continued to champion the #LeaveEveryPlaceBetter initiative, promoting 
sustainable practices across the Himalayan ecosystem.
ONE RIDE 2025
Royal Enfield brought together its global riding community for the 14th edition of 
One Ride in September 2025, uniting over 40,000 riders across 1,500 rides in 60+ 
countries. Celebrated as one of the largest annual motorcycling events in the world, the 
ride followed the sun across time zones – from the first sunrise in the East to the last 
sunset in the West – creating a seamless 24-hour global celebration. Bringing together 
riders of all backgrounds, the event highlighted individuality and self-expression 
while reinforcing the brand’s ethos of Pure Motorcycling. Alongside camaraderie and 
shared passion, One Ride 2025 also championed responsible riding through safe route 
planning, community mentorship, and safety-led initiatives such as 'Helmets for India'.

RIDING AHEAD OF THE CURVE
O P E R A T I N G C O N T E X T
The automobile world is shifting at pace, with rider aspirations evolving, 
focus on sustainable mobility growing and digital technologies 
penetrating across every aspect of operations. As a Company with a 
rich legacy that has ridden through multiple shifts and continues to 
be driven by an innovative mindset, EML stayed ahead of the curve, 
reading these trends early and responding with intent.
The results are evident: in a year when supply chains were tight, 
both Royal Enfield and VECV delivered their highest-ever volumes 
and consolidated market share, while contributing meaningfully to 
advancing the broader motorcycling industry. With each step forward, 
the Company is focussed on creating lasting value for all stakeholders 
while staying the fiercely differentiated brand that it is.
ASPIRATIONS FOR PREMIUM 
MOTORCYCLES
GLOBALISATION AND EMERGING 
MARKET EXPANSION
SUPPLY CHAIN LOCALISATION AND RESILIENCE
SURGE IN SUSTAINABLE AND 
ELECTRIC MOBILITY
DIGITISATION OF MOBILITY 
EXPERIENCE
Industry context:
Conflicts, disruptions, and shifting trade dynamics 
across the world have impacted supply chain 
continuity and cost efficiencies, necessitating localised 
sourcing and deepening supplier collaboration.
EML's strategic response:
Royal Enfield has pulled all levers of the supply chain to ensure 
resilience, including securing alternative vendors, prebuying 
and building inventory buffers, and optimising the variant-
feature mix. Further, aligned with its capacity expansion, the 
brand has been working alongside the vendor ecosystem 
to debottleneck areas and ramp up supplies to meet future 
demand. The localisation strategy extends globally through 
CKD operations that bring assembly closer to demand.
Industry context:
Globally, there is a rising shift toward mid-size, premium 
motorcycles, as riders seek experiences beyond mobility. 
Purpose, personality, performance, and distinctive design 
have become the new benchmarks and attributes for 
consumer decisions.
EML strategic response:
Royal Enfield continues to deliver premium experiences 
through innovative launches, thoughtful upgrades to its 
portfolio, and shaping experiences beyond motorcycles. In 
FY 2025-26, the brand introduced upgrades, including the 
2026 Guerrilla 450 Apex, Hunter 350, 2025 Meteor 350, 
2026 Goan Classic 350, and Himalayan Mana Black, each 
broadening appeal and deepening the brand's distinctive 
character. Royal Enfield's product quality leadership was 
validated in securing the highest rank in J.D. Power's 2026 
initial quality study in India. These efforts consolidated the 
brand’s market share to 86.8% in the domestic mid-size 
segment.
Industry context:
Green mobility, across both personal and commercial 
segments, is witnessing growing adoption amidst tightening 
emission regulations and rising consumer awareness. Factors 
like low cost of running also continue to attract consumers.
EML strategic response:
FY 2025-26 marked a breakthrough year for Royal Enfield 
in the electric urban mobility space, led by its dedicated 
City+ brand Flying Flea. The brand launched its first electric 
motorcycle, FF.C6 and also unveiled the scrambler-styled 
FF.S6. Flying Flea, through these motorcycles and more in 
the pipeline, is all set to take the Royal Enfield’s legacy into 
a new era.
VECV commercialised new electric and LNG trucks and 
buses. It also entered Charging Point Operator (CPO) 
agreements with strategic partners to strengthen the public 
charging network for wider adoption of its electric truck and 
bus portfolio.
Industry context:
Globally, aspirational and accessible motorcycles that 
come along with riding cultures and lifestyle-led choices 
are witnessing rising adoption as customers seek 
differentiated experiences.
EML strategic response:
In FY 2025-26, Royal Enfield strengthened its local 
presence across established and emerging markets in 
APAC, EMEA, the Latin America and the SAARC regions. 
The brand undertook several market-specific launches of 
its renowned motorcycles, including the Bear 650, Classic 
650, Hunter 350 and Scram 440. Further, across regions, 
the brand strengthened community, experiences, and 
riding culture through international and region-specific 
community rides, participation in marquee events, lifestyle 
partnerships, and retail network expansion.
Industry context:
Digital content integration into mobility and immersive digital 
experiences has evolved from a differentiator to a baseline 
expectation. Customers today are increasingly demanding 
experiences that are seamless, intuitive, and connected across 
all stages.
EML strategic response:
Royal Enfield has been at the forefront of integrating digital 
experiences across the riding experience, from exploring 
motorcycles on the website to customising them using Make-
it-Yours (MiY) and how it engages. The brand continues to 
make motorcycles more feature-rich with connected and smart 
mobility solutions such as navigation and ride telemetry. Social 
media is leveraged for sustained digital engagement, helping 
build affinity through content, conversation, and shared riding 
culture. In FY 2025-26, Royal Enfield partnered with Flipkart and 
Amazon India, enabling customers in select cities to purchase 
its 350cc range online through a seamless end-to-end digital 
journey, making ownership more accessible.

M A T E R I A L I T Y
TACKLING WHAT MATTERS FOR 
LONG-TERM VALUE
EML adopts a proactive approach to identifying and 
addressing material matters that could influence 
stakeholder interests and long-term business continuity.
RENEWING FOCUS ON ESG 
PRIORITIES
At EML, sustainability priorities continue 
to influence how the Company operates, 
collaborates with stakeholders, and 
makes investment decisions – ensuring 
alignment with evolving expectations and 
fostering resilience in an ever-changing 
landscape. EML’s ESG focus is shaped 
by the perspectives of its stakeholders, 
including customers, regulators, suppliers, 
employees, and community partners. 
The goal is to build a future that is 
environmentally responsible and socially 
inclusive.
In FY 2023-24, EML undertook a 
comprehensive review to refresh its ESG 
priorities. The issues identified are relevant 
for FY 2025-26. Drawing from current 
and emerging sustainability trends, the 
Company engaged with key stakeholder 
groups – through both digital and 
in-person interactions – to assess the 
relevance of 23 ESG themes and identify 
those requiring greater  focus.
The process involved feedback from 
seven stakeholder segments, including 
Royal Enfield employees and leadership, 
customers, investors, community 
partners, suppliers, and distributors. 
In addition, leadership insights helped 
evaluate the potential business impact 
and likelihood of these sustainability 
matters, enabling EML to prioritise actions 
that drive long-term value.
A STRUCTURED THREE-STEP APPROACH TO 
DEFINING ESG PRIORITIES
Shortlisting ESG Topics
A set of 23 ESG priority areas was identified through 
a thorough review of global sustainability frameworks 
such as S&P Corporate Sustainability Assessment (CSA), 
Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB), and 
Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI), along with 
benchmarking against industry peers.
Prioritisation through Stakeholder Engagement
Customised surveys – both online and offline – were 
rolled out across various stakeholder groups to 
capture insights on priority ESG topics. These targeted 
consultations yielded over 469 responses, offering 
a comprehensive view of what matters most to 
each  group.
Validation and Refinement
Findings from both primary and secondary 
engagements were analysed using a weighted 
average methodology to rank ESG priorities across 
all stakeholder groups, incorporating inputs from 
frameworks and peers. A leadership workshop was then 
conducted to validate and finalise the refreshed ESG 
priorities for Royal Enfield.

Cruise Control
Allows the rider to lock a specific speed without holding the throttle open, with one-
button activation on the switchgear. It supports comfort on long city flyovers and flat 
highway stretches.
Traction Control
Manages instant electric torque delivery of 60Nm. It reduces power to the motor 
when rear tyre slip is detected on wet asphalt, gravel or slick surfaces. The C6 offers 
three traction control levels that can be changed in Custom mode.
Cornering ABS (Anti lock 
braking system)
Uses an internal measurement sensor within the ABS unit to detect lean angle and 
dynamically alter braking pressure during mid-turn braking. This helps reduce the risk 
of the motorcycle standing up or sliding out under braking.
Bi-directional 
Crawl  Mode
Enables controlled low-speed movement in both forward and reverse directions, 
supporting ease of manoeuvring in tight parking spaces, slopes, and garages.
Auto-Hold
Holds the brakes automatically when the motorcycle stops on an incline. It activates 
when the brakes are held for two seconds and releases smoothly when the rider 
applies throttle.
Swappable Footpegs
Uses the clutchless automatic EV layout and handlebar rear brake to free the feet 
from control functions. The modular footpegs can be placed in the centre position for 
an upright commuter stance or moved forward for a relaxed cruiser layout.

Suspension

Digital technologies are strengthening the way we engage with

rider-focussed interfaces, EV readiness, data-led insights, and

our global community expects from us.
BUILDING AN INTEGRATED DIGITAL ECOSYSTEM
Our digital ecosystem is designed to connect the vehicle, rider, service network, charging infrastructure, and enterprise backend 
into one cohesive architecture. This approach allows us to support both petrol motorcycles and EV platforms with improved 
connectivity, diagnostics, personalisation, ride intelligence, and data security.
Android cluster for a smarter 
riding interface
We have developed a circular cluster 
powered by Android Automotive 
Operating System, bringing an enhanced 
interface and a comprehensive app 
ecosystem from Royal Enfield and third 
parties. The cluster extends beyond 
conventional display capability and 
supports essential EV functions, rider aids 
and navigation  features.
It includes a dynamic charging screen that 
accurately reflects charging states, along 
with a refined passcode entry system 
optimised for switchcube navigation. The 
interface also supports Cruise Control 
status indicators and Google Maps 
navigation mirroring, making the riding 
experience more intuitive and connected.
Wingman suite for connected 
mobility
The Wingman suite represents a 
significant extension of advanced 
telematics and connected vehicle 
capability across Royal Enfield’s EV and 
petrol motorcycles platforms. It enables 
us to bring core digital excellence into 
electric mobility while strengthening the 
connected ownership  experience.
Wingman integrates 4G LTE and GPS 
modules to enable live location tracking, 
remote vehicle status monitoring, and 
e-diagnostics for service technicians. 
Riders can access information linked 
to ignition, battery, and signal strength, 
supporting greater transparency 
and  convenience.
The suite also includes patented features 
such as SOS support, remote lock 
and unlock, and vehicle and charger 
configuration. These features work in 
collaboration with the Android Automotive 
cluster, creating a more seamless 
interaction between the motorcycle, rider, 
and digital interface.
Strengthening security and 
ride  intelligence
Security is a core part of our connected 
vehicle architecture. Wingman includes 
two-factor authentication for engine 
activation, geofencing with entry and 
exit alerts, and Tow Away or tampering 
notifications. These features are designed 
to enhance rider confidence and 
strengthen vehicle protection.
Our trip intelligence capability has 
also been refined to provide more 
accurate trip reporting. It analyses 
harsh acceleration, braking and lean 
angles, while allowing riders to merge 
or unmerge auto-generated trips. This 
supports a richer understanding of riding 
patterns and improves the overall digital 
ownership  experience.
Enabling EV readiness through 
digital platforms
As we advance our EV journey, digital 
systems are becoming integral to product 
performance, charging, diagnostics, 
and user experience. Our charging 
ecosystem development covers home, 
public, and dealer charging infrastructure, 
grid support and the Charging 
Diagnostics  Application.
These capabilities support the transition 
to connected electric mobility by 
enabling better charging visibility, service 
readiness, and integration across vehicle 
and infrastructure layers. Together with 
app-based controls, remote features and 
backend intelligence, they help create a 
more complete EV ecosystem.
Cloud, data, and backend intelligence
Our cloud and backend systems provide 
the intelligence layer that supports 
connected mobility at scale. Data lake 
integration through BigQuery enables 
structured data management and 
analytics. Predictive maintenance models 
are being developed to improve service 
foresight and vehicle health monitoring.
We are also building feature and 
subscription management capabilities 
through a microservices architecture. 
This allows us to support scalable digital 
features, flexible product experiences, and 
faster deployment of future digital services.
Digital trust and governance
As our connected ecosystem grows, 
security and governance remain central 
to our digital approach. We are aligning 
our systems with General Data Protection 
Regulation requirements, strengthening 
data privacy protocols, and embedding 
Security Shift-Left practices into 
development.
This means security considerations are 
integrated earlier in the development 
cycle, helping us identify and address risks 
before deployment. Through this approach, 
we are building digital platforms that are 
connected, scalable, and trusted.
Connecting the next phase of mobility
Our digital capability is strengthening

connected mobility. By integrating

Transitioning to Advanced Aquatron-RFOD 
Water Technology
In line with our commitment to sustainable 
manufacturing practices, Royal Enfield is currently 
in the process of implementing Aquatron-
Reduction Facilitated Osmotic Diffusion (RFOD), 
a pioneering water-treatment technology that 
marks a significant leap forward at our Zero Liquid 
Discharge (ZLD) capabilities in our Vallam Vadagal 
Vadagal manufacturing unit. This advanced 
system utilises cutting-edge molecular-breaking 
resonance technology to revolutionise our effluent 
management. By transitioning to this innovative 
process, we are completely eliminating the 
energy-intensive RO3, RO4, and RO5 skids, as well 
as our traditional evaporator plant operations. 
The Aquatron system efficiently breaks down 
polluting compounds to recover high-quality 
potable water, delivering dual benefits of ecological 
responsibility and operational efficiency. Once fully 
commissioned, this upgrade is projected to achieve 
an annual industrial Reverse Osmosis (Industrial 
Reverse Osmosis) water saving of 3,600 KL and 
a recurring cost saving of C 9 Lakhs per annum, 
further decoupling our production growth from our 
environmental footprint.

MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION

ECONOMIC OVERVIEW
Indian Economy
India retained its position as one of the world's fastest-growing 
major economies in FY 2025-26, with Real GDP growth 
estimated at 7.6%, accelerating from the 7.1% in FY 2024-25. 
Strong domestic consumption, public capital expenditure, and 
resilient services exports drove the expansion, with agriculture 
supported by a favourable monsoon. In US dollar terms, 
India's GDP stood at approximately USD 3.92 Trillion, with 
the economy placed sixth in global rankings, reflecting the 
impact of rupee depreciation and a statistical revision of the 
GDP base year, rather than any underlying slowdown. Inflation 
remained benign through the year, supported by a prolonged 
decline in food prices. Consumer Price Index (CPI) eased 
to 3.4% by March 2026, well within the RBI’s target band, 
prompting the central bank to reduce the repo rate to 5.25% 
to support growth.

Global Economy
Global economic growth remained moderate in Financial Year 
2026, with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) projecting 
global output growth at around 3.1%. Escalating geopolitical 
tensions in the Middle East, elevated trade uncertainty, energy 
market disruptions, and tighter financial conditions weighed on 
global trade, investment activity, and business sentiment across 
regions. However, resilient services activity and technology-led 
investments provided partial support to economic momentum.
Global inflation, after easing through 2025, witnessed renewed 
pressure during 2026 due to higher energy and food prices 
arising from supply-side disruptions. The IMF expects global 
headline inflation to rise to around 4.4% in 2026 before 
moderating gradually. In major developed economies such as 
the USA, the UK, Europe, Australia and Japan, inflation remained 
relatively stable within the range of 2%-3.5%, enabling selective 
monetary easing in certain markets. Meanwhile, several 
emerging economies continued to face elevated inflation, 
currency volatility, and tighter monetary conditions, resulting in 
sustained higher interest rates across   markets.
Source: IMF, World Economic Outlook April 2026
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
Indian Two-Wheeler Industry
The two-wheeler segment posted its highest-ever annual 
sales in FY 2025-26 of 2.17 Crore units, with a growth of 
10.7% over FY 2024-25, crossing the previous peak of 2.12 
Crore units achieved in FY 2018-19, as per SIAM (Society 
of Indian Automobile Manufacturers). The implementation 
of GST 2.0, repo rate cuts, and income tax relief provided 
a strong impetus to consumer demand, though growth 
was back-ended for the two-wheeler industry. First half of 
FY 2025-26 (H1) was flat at sub 1%, while Second half posted 
growth of approximately 21.5%. The exports of two-wheelers 
from India recorded highest ever mark at 51.8 lakh units in 
FY 2025‑26, marking a growth of 23.4% over last year, driven 
by a wider product range, growing global recognition of Indian 
two‑wheeler brands, and support from a depreciated rupee as 
per  SIAM. 
Source: SIAM's official press release dated 14 April 2026
Global Motorcycle Industry
The global motorcycle industry continued its upward 
trajectory in 2025, with worldwide sales reaching 65.2 Million 
units, reflecting a 4.7% year-on-year growth despite ongoing 
macroeconomic uncertainties. India retained its position as 
the world’s largest motorcycle market, supported by sustained 
domestic demand and continued premiumisation trends, while 
Latin America and ASEAN markets also recorded healthy 
momentum during the year.
The premium motorcycle segment witnessed strong traction, 
driven by rising demand for lower-displacement motorcycles, 
adventure touring, and lifestyle-led mobility experiences. 
Simultaneously, electric two-wheelers continued gaining 
global acceptance as manufacturers accelerated investments 
in cleaner and technology-led mobility solutions. India’s two-
wheeler exports remained robust during the year, supported by 
deeper market penetration across Africa, Latin America, and 
other emerging international markets.

two‑wheeler segment. Royal Enfield Motorcycles are engaging, 
uncomplicated, accessible, and fun to ride; a vehicle for 
exploration and self-expression. It’s an approach the brand calls 
Pure Motorcycling.

Emission management 
During the year, the Company further reduced its emission 
footprint from 29.1 to 23.5 (tCO2e per motorcycle produced), 
continuing to explore new ways of achieving resource 
efficiency and environmental protection. The Company 
has also disclosed its Scope 1 and 2 emissions as part 
of the integrated report this year to better estimate the 
overall emission footprint and draw a path to Net Zero. 
Focussed interventions helped reduce Scope 1 & 2 emissions 
by 19% during the year.
Water management 
The Company continued to maintain Zero Liquid Discharge 
across all its operations. It has implemented rainwater 
harvesting systems and sewage treatment plants, the water 
from which is used for various applications. EML ensures 
providing water access to the surrounding community and 
natural ecosystem. The new Cheyyar facility is water positive 
and has been operating as a zero liquid discharge plant since 
inception, underscoring the Company's commitment to 
responsible resource management.
Waste management 
Ensuring a circular economy, the Company adopted the 
principles of 'Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle' across all 
operational activities. All facilities are zero liquid discharge 
factories where wastewater is treated in state-of-the-art STP 
and ETP plants and reused for irrigation and process top-ups. 
The Company has significantly reduced plastic consumption 
in packaging and has achieved zero waste to landfill status. 
The Company has also commenced the usage of Compressed 
Biogas in operations at the Vallam Vadagal plant.
Supply and Packaging
To drive a more sustainable value chain, the Company has 
transitioned to Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) certified 
suppliers for its carton packaging. During the year, the 
Company achieved nearly 100% sustainable packaging 
across its Genuine Motorcycle Accessories range, with all 
carton boxes now sustainably sourced. Furthermore, within 
the parts packaging segment, the Company successfully 
eliminated 85% of single-use plastic covers, replacing them 
with biodegradable and compostable alternatives.
Dr. Shroff’s Charity Eye Hospital:
Since 1996, a long-standing partnership with 
Dr. Shroff's Charity Eye Hospital (SCEH) has supported the 
institution's journey from strengthening governance to 
enhancing day-to-day clinical operations. During the year, 
support enabled the installation of over 300 CCTV cameras 
across the main hospital and its network of 44 vision centres 
across North India, strengthening safe and secure healthcare 
delivery for more than 28,000 people. The partnership 
continues to evolve in line with regional public health priorities.
Royal Enfield Academy for Technical Skills:
The Academy for Technical Skills continued to equip young 
people in Tamil Nadu with industry-relevant technical training, 
practical exposure and essential workplace skills. During FY 
2025–26, the Academy trained 1,065 candidates and 
achieved a 99% placement rate across the automotive 
industry, meeting its annual training target within the first 
six months. The initiative continues to create sustainable 
livelihood opportunities while strengthening the future-ready 
automotive workforce.
2. Brand-led Social Mission
2 projects on Healthcare and Education, which have the 
higher allocation of CSR spend. Royal Enfield’s Social Mission 
stems from the 75-year-old connection with its Spiritual 
Home of the Himalayas. Operating at the intersection of 
Culture, Conservation, and Materiality, the mission is on track 
to meet its long-term vision of partnering 100 Himalayan 
communities by 2030 towards building climate resilience.
Some of the notable projects and initiatives 
this year includes:
Himalayan Hub
A collective learning centre dedicated to developing 
solutions for environmental sustainability in the Indian 
Himalayan Region. The Hub works to equip Himalayan 
youth to become leaders in climate change mitigation 
and adaptation – through fellowships, grants, and 
structured programmes – while building resilience within 
their communities.
Green Pit Stops
An initiative that creates livelihood opportunities for local 
communities while offering environment-friendly amenities 
to tourists – including clean drinking water, sanitation, 
waste management, hygienic local food, charging facilities, 
service check-points, and local handicrafts. These centres 
are managed by Self-Help Groups (predominantly women) 
and serve as shared spaces where local communities 
and travellers can connect. Designed sustainably using 
vernacular architecture, the pit-stops also function 
as showcases and marketplaces for local handicrafts, 
art, and culture.
The Himalayan Knot
A market linkage programme supporting Himalayan artisan 
communities practising traditional crafts – weaving, 
knitting, and working with natural fibres such as pashmina, 
wool, eri silk, and cotton. The programme spotlights their 
craft through design interventions and communication 
campaigns, expanding market access and strengthening 
livelihoods. The programme also supports the conservation 
of pastures and rangelands, protecting the livestock of 
vulnerable pastoral communities, and building skills for 
value-added livelihoods such as dairy and cheese-making, 
thereby taking a holistic approach to conserve local 
heritage and reduce out-migration from the Himalayas.
The Great Himalayan Exploration
A behaviour change initiative that raises awareness and 
positively shapes tourist attitudes on environmental and 
social issues, this programme creates active opportunities 
for riders and travellers to engage with and contribute to 
CSR-led initiatives. Supported by targeted Information, 
Education, and Communication (IEC) packs, these initiatives 
include documentation of Intangible Cultural Heritage 
(ICH) practices in partnership with UNESCO through 
rider researchers, and working with remote communities. 
To expand reach and deepen impact, the programme is 
scaling its content dissemination efforts in collaboration with 
National Geographic, set to air on television and JioHotstar. 
Concurrently, strategic partnerships are being explored with 
the Wikimedia Foundation, Ministry of Tourism, travel media 
such as Condé Nast, Himalayan state tourism boards, and 
academic institutions to amplify the programme’s footprint 
across knowledge, policy, and cultural platforms.
Keystone Species
The programme works to conserve the critical habitat and 
unique biodiversity in the landscapes inhabited by the Snow 
Leopard. The species has deep significance for the indigenous 
and pastoral communities across five states and Ladakh UT 
and is a keystone species in the high altitude regions of the 
Himalayas. Its presence and survival directly influences local 
biodiversity and shapes the population dynamics of other 
species in the ecosystem.
Beyond the Snow Leopard, the programme extends its reach 
to the conservation of other critical landscapes, ecosystems, 
and species in the region besides coastal and aquatic habitat 
– with community stewardship at the heart of this effort.
Through the Social Mission, Royal Enfield is also aspiring to 
encourage and inspire one million riders to explore sustainably 
and ‘Leave every place better’.

INTERNAL CONTROL SYSTEMS AND THEIR ADEQUACY
The Company has instituted a robust and well-integrated 
internal control system designed to ensure operational 
efficiency, asset protection, accurate financial reporting, 
and strict compliance with applicable laws and regulations. 
This internal control framework serves as a safeguard against 
unauthorised usage or loss of assets, helps in the early 
detection and prevention of fraud, and supports precision 
in financial disclosures. It also enables the Company to 
address emerging business risks and maintain productivity 
across operations.
In FY 2025-26, the Company undertook a comprehensive 
evaluation of its internal controls over financial reporting and 
concluded that these were adequate and operating effectively. 
As part of its ongoing commitment to strengthening 
governance mechanisms, the Company continued its 
initiative, Internal Control, Centre of Excellence (IC-CoE), a 
specialised project aimed at enhancing control measures 
across critical functions. The IC-CoE operates as a centralised 
expert unit, offering continuous advisory support and 
facilitating consistent process-level oversight. It works closely 
with project and process owners to ensure that accountability, 
control adherence, and governance standards are upheld 
across the organisation.
The Company’s SAP-based Enterprise Resource 
Planning (ERP) system acts as a critical backbone 
for enforcing system-driven controls and validations. 
This technology-driven approach ensures real-time tracking, 
data integrity, and minimises manual intervention, thereby 
reducing risks associated with human error.
Additionally, EML has implemented comprehensive 
governance, risk, and compliance frameworks that reinforce 
the effectiveness of its internal control environment. 
These frameworks help ensure that the Company’s operations 
align with statutory and regulatory requirements at all times.
An independent Internal Audit team carries out periodic 
reviews of processes and functions, as per the annual 
audit plan approved by the Audit Committee. These audits 
are instrumental in evaluating the health of the control 
mechanisms and recommending improvements where needed. 
The statutory auditors also review the adequacy of internal 
financial controls as part of their audit procedures related to 
financial reporting.
The Company’s Whistle-Blower Policy and Vigil Mechanism 
further strengthen its governance ecosystem by empowering 
employees, vendors, dealers, and other stakeholders to 
report any unethical practices, fraud, or misconduct without 
fear of retaliation. This encourages transparency, reinforces 
accountability, and supports a culture of integrity across 
the organisation.

outlines the overarching process for managing crises, 
covering actions, escalation protocols, and communication 
strategies. All relevant stakeholders, including process/
project owners and crisis response team members across 
various departments, are required to read and understand 
the processes and escalation matrices within this handbook. 
This ensures an effective response to any crisis situation. 
The timely management and effective communication with 
stakeholders during a crisis are crucial for minimising the 
impact on business operations.

FINANCIAL REVIEW
Eicher Motors Limited achieved its highest-ever annual volumes in FY 2025–26 at 1,227,977 units. Revenue for the year 
increased by 24% year-on-year to ` 23,408 Crores, marking yet another milestone as the highest-ever annual revenue 
recorded by the Company.
A great acceptance and rising penetration of aftermarket parts and services, greater availability of genuine motorcycle 
accessories, and a wider range of apparel underpinned a healthy performance of the allied business. Total revenue from spares 
and services, apparel, accessories, and others increased to C 3,351 Crores in 2025‑26 and contributed to 14.5% of EML’s 
consolidated revenues.
Earnings before Interest, Tax, Depreciation and Amortisation (EBITDA) of the Company increased by 23% to C 5,785 Crores 
in 2025-26 from C 4,712 Crores in 2024-25. EBITDA percentage for the year was 24.7% in 2025-26 as against 
25% in 2024-25.
Consolidated Net Profit After Tax (PAT) increased by 16.5% 
to C 5,515 Crores in FY 2025-26 from C 4,734 Crores in 
FY 2024-25. An increase in Revenue, EBITDA, and higher 
contribution from the Company's JV with Volvo AB - Volvo 
Eicher Commercial Vehicles have uplifted the profit growth 
over the last year. As a result, EML's consolidated EPS (Basic) 
for the year increased by 16% to C 201.1 per share.
The Company's financial position remains robust with total 
cash and cash equivalents, and investments (other than 
in subsidiaries and Joint Ventures) of C 19,091 Crores. 
It generated a healthy cash flow from operations at C 4,805 
Crores and continued to invest in its future—which includes 
new product development activities (both petrol motorcycles 
and EVs) and setting up operation facilities along with a special 
focus on growing its digital capabilities. The total capital 
investment for the year stood at C 1,275 Crores.

Business Environment
India continued to remain among the fastest-growing 
major economies during FY 2025-26, supported by strong 
consumer confidence, sustained public infrastructure 
investments, and stable tax collections. Despite geopolitical 
uncertainties in West Asia and temporary disruptions in 
fuel and commodity supplies during March, the economy 
demonstrated resilience and maintained growth momentum.
The Commercial Vehicle (CV) industry continued to benefit 
from structural reforms, improving logistics infrastructure, and 
rising economic activity. Overall CV industry volumes, including 
exports, grew by 13% year-on-year to reach a new peak of 
1.20 Million units.
Government initiatives focussed on improving logistics 
efficiency, transportation safety, and accelerating clean 
mobility adoption. Programmes such as PM Gati Shakti, 
smart tolling systems, the Unified Logistics Interface Platform 
(ULIP), enhanced PM e-Drive funding, and expanded 
Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes supported 
fleet modernisation, technology adoption, and long-term 
industry growth.
Regulatory and Digital Logistics Shift
The industry also witnessed continued regulatory evolution 
aimed at improving safety, sustainability, and fleet 
modernisation. Stricter implementation of vehicle scrappage 
norms, mandatory air-conditioned cabins for trucks from 
June 2025, and higher safety standards such as Fire Detection 
and Suppression Systems (FDSS) in buses are expected to 
further accelerate replacement demand and raise operational 
benchmarks across the sector.
VECV Performance
FY 2025-26 marked a landmark year for VECV as the Company 
crossed the milestone of 1,00,000 annual vehicle sales for 
the first time, recording sales of 1,03,404 trucks and buses. 
Volumes grew by 14.7% over the previous year, ahead of the 
overall industry growth of 13%, reflecting strong execution, 
customer-centricity, operational excellence, and continued 
technology advancement.
Key highlights during the year included:
	 Eicher-branded trucks and buses crossed the 1,00,000-unit 
milestone, with sales of 1,00,980 units. Including Volvo 
trucks and buses, total VECV sales stood at 1,03,404 units. 
	 The LMD segment retained market leadership with a 34.9% 
market share, while the Heavy Duty segment achieved 
its highest-ever annual sales of 26,867 units with a 
9.7% market share. 
	 Bus sales stood at 19,363 units, including 208 
electric buses. 
	 The Company launched the Eicher Pro X diesel range, with 
final assembly carried out at an all-women production line at 
Bhopal, reinforcing its commitment to workplace inclusion. 
	 Product innovation remained strong with over 100 
new models and variants launched, 252 patents filed, 
and more than 3,300 ideas generated through the 
innovation platform. 
	 Key launches included the Eicher Pro 8035XM 8x4 mining 
tipper with AMT and a 29.5 cubic metre body, along with 
India’s first 25.25-metre Volvo FM 420 road-train trailer 
configuration. 
	 Electric and LNG offerings were further expanded across 
truck and bus segments. 
	 The network expanded by 164 touchpoints to reach 
1,250 outlets. Company-owned dealer operations grew 
to 20  main hubs with 140 touchpoints, selling over 
17,200  units during the year. 
	 Manufacturing operations achieved record production of 
1,02,452 vehicles, supported by automation, advanced 
robotics, Industrial IoT, AI-driven quality controls, and the 
Volvo Production System. 
	 Digital and service capabilities continued to strengthen, 
with the MyEicher platform expanding to over 1,85,000 
customers, predictive analytics under Superior Uptime 
proactively preventing thousands of potential vehicle 
issues, and Site Support expanding to 430 sites covering 
over 23,500 vehicles. 
	 Employee engagement improved significantly, with the 
engagement score increasing to 85 from 80. 
	 The Company received seven recognitions at the 17th 
Apollo CV Awards, including 
	
	 CV Maker of the Year”, “Debutant of the Year” 
for Eicher Pro X, 
	
	 School Bus of the Year, 
	
	 LCV Cargo Carrier of the Year (Up to 7.5T),
	
	 CV Transport Solution Provider of the Year, 
	
	 CV Innovation of the Year” for Volvo Road Train, and
	
	 CV Communications Excellence of the Year”. 
Overall, VECV remained agile and customer-focussed while 
continuing to strengthen its role in modernising commercial 
transportation in India and beyond.

ETB delivered another record year, crossing the milestone of 
1 lakh vehicles produced and delivered during FY 2025-26. 
The LMD segment (5-18T) further strengthened its leadership 
position with sales of 46,195 units and a market share of 
34.9%, reflecting year-on-year growth of 19.4%.
The HD segment delivered its highest-ever annual sales at 
25,155 units, with market share improving to 9.1%. Bus sales 
stood at 18,651 units, supported by continued scale-up in 
electric buses.

manufacturing facilities, with total production reaching

A brief on types of customers
	
	
Eicher Motors Limited (EML) serves a diverse and evolving customer base, comprising individual riders, commercial 
enterprises, and government agencies. Through its flagship brand, Royal Enfield, the Company continues to maintain a 
strong position in the premium motorcycle segment. Supported by a versatile product portfolio and a steadfast focus 
on quality, the Company attracts a broad spectrum of customers with varied preferences, aspirations, and mobility 
requirements.
	
Key Customer Segments
	
Motorcycling Enthusiasts
	
These customers are drawn to Royal Enfield’s distinctive design language, heritage-inspired styling, and character of its 
motorcycles. They value the brand’s legacy, authenticity, and riding experience alongside performance and craftsmanship.
	
Adventure Seekers
	
Royal Enfield’s adventure touring and off-road motorcycles cater to riders seeking exploration and long-distance travel. 
Equipped with robust chassis, capable suspension systems, and terrain-ready features, these motorcycles support diverse 
riding conditions and expedition-style journeys.
	
Daily Commuters
	
Designed to offer comfort, reliability, and ease of handling, Royal Enfield motorcycles provide a practical mobility solution 
for everyday use. Their manoeuvrability, rider comfort, and dependable performance make them well-suited for urban and 
inter-city commuting.
	
Retro and Classic Motorcycle Enthusiasts 
	
Royal Enfield continues to appeal to customers who appreciate classic styling, timeless design, and heritage-inspired 
motorcycling. Its portfolio combines traditional aesthetics with contemporary engineering, catering to riders seeking a 
distinctive retro motorcycling experience.

Product Design & Circular Economy: 
	
As part of our commitment to life-cycle sustainability and extended producer responsibility, the Company actively integrates 
circular economy principles into end-of-life product management. Our strategy focusses on enhancing product circularity 
right from the initial design phase to regulated, safe disposal pathways.
	
The Product Development team continuously evaluate and conduct feasibility studies aimed at identifying and substituting 
conventional materials with sustainable, alternate materials across our motorcycle components.
	
Demonstrating leadership in circular product design, the Company is the first automotive Original Equipment Manufacturer 
(OEM) to conduct a formal (RRR) Recyclability, Recoverability, and Reusability assessment for its motorcycles. This 
evaluation establishes a new sustainable design benchmark in the industry, with third-party assessments demonstrating high 
mass efficiency metrics across our primary models:

Internal Operational & Manufacturing Waste
	
Our manufacturing operations generate hazardous, non-hazardous, and electronic waste streams, all of which are 
managed in strict accordance with applicable national environmental regulations. To ensure absolute compliance with legal 
frameworks, all waste management processes are executed on-site by our respective manufacturing plants.
	
Waste streams generated across the facilities are systematically segregated at the source within individual production lines. 
Following categorisation and volume compilation, these materials are directed into dedicated compliance pathways:
	
	
Plastics & Packaging: All plastic waste is channelled exclusively to Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) authorised 
recyclers, ensuring full traceability and the subsequent generation of Extended Producer Responsibility certificates
 
	
Hazardous & Other Wastes: These streams are securely routed to authorised recyclers or re-processors for 
material recovery. Where material recycling is not viable, the waste is directed to co-processing units within authorised 
cement plants for sustainable energy recovery

The main Social Mission projects include ‘The Himalayan Knot’ — a textile conservation project, bringing together pastoral

10.	 Briefly describe the waste management practices adopted in your establishments. Describe the strategy 
adopted by your company to reduce usage of hazardous and toxic chemicals in your products and processes 
and the practices adopted to manage such wastes.
	
The Company has a structured waste management system to manage manufacturing and operational waste across its 
establishments. The Company follows the principles of Reduce, Reuse and Recycle (3Rs) and promotes circularity by 
reducing waste generation, encouraging reuse / recycling and minimising the use of virgin materials. Waste generated 
is classified into hazardous and non-hazardous, as well as recyclable and non-recyclable categories, and is managed 
through defined processes covering identification, segregation, collection, recycling, and safe disposal. Hazardous and 
other applicable wastes are disposed of through CPCB-authorised vendors, in compliance with applicable local regulatory 
requirements. The Company is also working towards Zero Waste to Landfill (ZWL) and promotes waste reduction practices 
among employees across facilities, supported by initiatives such as a paperless work culture. The Company’s operations are 
covered under an ISO 14001:2015 certified environmental management system.
	
With respect to hazardous and toxic chemicals, the Company is committed to reducing their usage in products and 
processes wherever feasible through process improvements, material optimisation, and safer handling practices. Such 
wastes are identified, segregated, stored, and disposed of safely through authorised channels in accordance with applicable 
environmental norms.

The Company’s Remuneration Policy:
The Company’s Compensation Strategy defines the principles 
underlying the compensation philosophy for its employees. 
Compensation is a critical piece of the overall human-
resources strategy and broadly refers to all forms of financial 
returns and tangible benefits that employees receive as a 
part of their employment relationship.
The Remuneration/Compensation Policy of the Company is 
designed to attract, motivate and retain its employees. This 
Policy applies to Directors and Senior Management including 
Key Managerial Personnel (KMP) and other employees of 
the Company.
The remuneration of the Managing Director, Whole-time/ 
Executive Director, Key Managerial Personnel (KMPs) and 
Senior Management of the Company is recommended by the 
Nomination and Remuneration Committee based on criteria 
such as industry benchmarks, the Company’s performance 
vis-à-vis the industry, individual’s responsibilities and 
performance assessment. The Company pays remuneration 
by way of salary, perquisites and allowances (fixed 
component), incentive remuneration and/or commission 
(variable components).
Loans/advances may be extended to employees for various 
personal purposes or to aid business functions, from time 
to time, on a case-to-case basis, in accordance with the 
relevant Human Resource guidelines/policies in force or 
as may be approved by the Chief Financial Officer, the 
Chief Human Resource Officer of the Company, or any 
person authorised by them, including for relocation (school 
deposits/expenses, travel/logistics expenses, housing 
advance, housing deposits/brokerage, any other expenses 
towards relocation); advance submission of tax deducted at 
source by the Company on behalf of the employee; advance 
towards medical insurance premiums; loans granted to 
enable grantees exercise ESOPs and towards deposit of 
perquisite tax thereon; loans/advances covered under the 
Employees Union recognised by the Company as per Union 
Agreement; medical emergency advances, etc.
Additionally, in the event of exigencies arising due to 
calamities, the Company may provide financial assistance 
to any affected employee by way of extending interest-free 
loan of an amount not exceeding the employee’s two months’ 
gross salary.
Remuneration by way of commission to the Non-Executive 
Directors is decided by the Board of Directors within the limit 
of 1% of the annual net profits of the Company in each of the 
financial years, calculated in accordance with Section 197, 198 
of the Act.
Remuneration of KMPs and employees largely consists of 
basic remuneration, perquisites, allowances, performance 
incentives and employee stock options granted pursuant 
to the Employees Stock Option Plan, 2006 and Restricted 
Stock Units Plan, 2019 of the Company. The components 
of remuneration vary for different employee levels and are 
governed by industry patterns, qualifications and experience 
of the employee and employee(s) responsibility areas, 
performance assessment, etc.

Enfield outside India which is also ISO 9001:14000 certified. 
During the FY 2025-26, RETH achieved assembling eight (8) 
Royal Enfield motorcycle models through its CKD assembly 
facility, reinforcing its presence in the Thailand market. The 
Company also commenced exports to Vietnam and initiated 
rim assembly for supply to Eicher Motors Limited and Royal 
Enfield Brasil Comercio de Motocicleta Ltda.
RETH continued to strengthen its presence in Thailand and is 
represented through a dealer network of 28 exclusive stores, 
one multi-brand outlet and seven authorised sales and 
service points. Royal Enfield maintained its position as the 
second-largest player in the mid-size motorcycle segment in 
Thailand, with a market share of 19.3% during the FY 2025-26. 
Royal Enfield continues to enjoy strong acceptance amongst 
customers, riding communities, dealer partners, custom 
builders and rental operators, supported by more than 60 
Royal Enfield communities across the country.
During the FY 2025-26, RETH received two awards from the 
Grand Prix Group, with the Goan Classic 350 being recognised 
as the “Best Modern Classic” and the Super Meteor 650 
receiving the “Modern Cruiser Middleweight” award. The 
Company sold 3,161 motorcycles during the FY 2025-26 and 
recorded revenue of ` 169.94 Crores, representing a growth of 
43.7% over the previous financial year.
Royal Enfield UK Ltd
(Wholly-owned Subsidiary)
Royal Enfield UK Ltd. (“REUK”) was incorporated in August 
2019 and commenced sales operations in June 2020. REUK 
commenced direct sales to the local dealers in the United 
Kingdom (“UK”), without a local distributor, from May, 2023. As 
at March 31, 2026, REUK had 51 sales and aftersales partners, 
including 18 exclusive stores in the UK. As part of its network 
development plans, REUK appointed leading dealer partners 
and continued the development of new dealerships for the 
forthcoming financial year.
During the FY 2025-26, REUK sold 3,292 motorcycles and 
recorded revenue of ` 154.84 Crores, representing growth of 
11% over the previous financial year. Royal Enfield achieved 
the No. 2 position in the mid-size motorcycle segment 
by market share in the UK. During the FY 2025-26, Royal 
Enfield was ranked No. 2 in the National Motorcycle Dealer 
Association’s manufacturer-dealer relationship survey.
Royal Enfield Europe B.V.

March 2024 and commenced sales operations from July 
2025. RE Europe started selling directly in the Germany 
market without a local distributor from October 2025. It has a

in some Eastern European countries.

Impact Assessment 1:
	
Project: Local Area Development
	
CSR initiative: Skill Development — Don Bosco Tech 
Society, Lucknow
	
Impact assessment carried out by: Sambodhi 
Research and Communications Private Limited
	
The Company had partnered with Don Bosco Tech 
Society to deliver centre-based residential automotive 
skills training for marginalised youth in Lucknow, Uttar 
Pradesh from 2022 to 2024. The programme covered 
four automotive job roles including Two-Wheeler Service 
Technician and Automotive Sales Executive, combined 
with on-the-job training at Royal Enfield dealerships, 
Automotive Skill Development Council-aligned 
certification, and post-placement support.
	
Findings — 49% of the participants secured employment 
post-training, out of which 85.7% were placed in roles 
aligned to their training. Median starting salary rose from 
` 12,109 to ` 17,718 among retained trainees. Among the 
49% participants who secured employment post training, 
household income improved significantly, with nearly all 
the placed trainees reporting increased financial stability. 
98.6% of respondents fell in the moderate-to-high 
self-esteem range on the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale, 
with placed trainees scoring the highest. Non-monetary 
impacts were significant, with 83.3% reporting improved 
confidence and 89.3% stating they had become 
financially independent.
	
Impact Assessment 2:
	
Project: Local Area Development
	
CSR initiative: Skill Development — Royal Enfield Skill 
Development Centre, Coimbatore
	
Impact assessment carried out by: Sambodhi 
Research and Communications Private Limited
	
The Company supported the Skill Development Centre 
at Akshaya College of Engineering and Technology, 
Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu, providing residential 
automotive skills training to approximately 600 youth 
from semi-urban and semi-rural backgrounds from 
January 2023 to May 2024. The programme covered 
curriculum design, Automotive Skill Development Council 
(ASDC)-aligned certification, placement facilitation, and 
post-placement tracking.
	
Findings — 92.8% of participants secured employment 
post-training, the highest placement rate across all 
projects being assessed. Median personal income rose 
from ` 12,000 to ` 16,000, and 26.7% of the trainees 
earned above ` 20,000. The proportion of households 
earning below ` 10,000 per month fell from 46.4% 
to 5.2% following the training, reflecting significant 
household-level economic uplift. 96.6% of trainees 
completed on-the-job training, the highest on-the-job 
training completion rate in the portfolio. 91% reported 
improved confidence and 96.7% reported increased 
work-related mobility. The programme demonstrated 
measurable and sustained economic transformation at 
household level.
	
Impact Assessment 3:
	
Project: Education
	
CSR initiative: Education — Shikshak Pahal 
Programme, Alwar
	
Impact assessment carried out by: Sambodhi 
Research and Communications Private Limited
	
The Company supported Bodh Shiksha Samiti (BSS) to 
deliver foundational schooling across 32 Bodhshalas in 
Thanagazi and Umrein Blocks, Alwar District, Rajasthan, 
serving approximately 4,688 students. Interventions 
covered teacher capacity building, contextual Teaching-
Learning Material (TLM) development, supplementary 
nutrition, digital infrastructure, and community 
engagement from 2023 to 2025.
	
Findings — 88.7% of programme students read at story 
level by Class 5, compared to 53.6% in control schools 
and 47.6% for the Rajasthan state average. 69.4% of 
programme students reached division-level numeracy 
by Class 5, versus 33.9% in control schools. The teacher 
quality was significantly higher with 88% of teachers 
in programme schools received structured training 
compared to 30% in control schools, and 96% of the 
teachers developed or adapted their own teaching-
learning materials. The programme demonstrated 
sustained mastery, not merely grade-level compliance,

Impact Assessment 4:
	
Project: Local Area Development/ Education
	
CSR initiative: Child-Safe School Environment — Rural 
Education and Action for Liberation, Cuddalore
	
Impact assessment carried out by: Sambodhi 
Research and Communications Private Limited
	
The Company supported the Rural Education and Action 
for Liberation (REAL) project in Cuddalore District, Tamil 
Nadu, from June 2023 to June 2024. Key interventions 
included construction of 9 new classrooms, provision 
of school toilets in three schools, installation of RO 
water purifiers in four schools, incinerators in two middle 
schools, and child-friendly Information, Education and 
Communication (IEC) wall paintings across 4 villages.
	
Findings — 100% of students reported visible 
improvements in classroom infrastructure. Reflecting 
universal positive perception of upgraded facilities. 
99.2% of students confirmed adequate seating and 
electricity availability. The infrastructure has directly 
contributed to improved classroom discipline, sustained 
student attention, and enhanced teacher effectiveness. 
The intervention successfully created safe, hygienic, and 
child-friendly learning environments serving all students 
across the four target villages.
	
Impact Assessment 5:
	
Project: Himalayan Hub
	
CSR initiative: Solid Waste Management — Waste 
Warriors, Jim Corbett
	
Impact assessment carried out by: Sambodhi 
Research and Communications Private Limited
	
The Company supported Waste Warriors in establishing 
a door-to-door waste collection system in Jim Corbett, 
Uttarakhand, from December 2021 to November 2024. 
The programme trained and empowered women-led 
Self-Help Groups (Paryavaran Sakhis) to manage waste 
collection, instituted a user-fee model, and set up waste 
processing infrastructure in collaboration with local 
government.
	
Findings — 99% community awareness was recorded, 
with 100% of households handing over waste to 
authorised collectors and 99% willing to continue paying 
user fees. Waste burning was completely eliminated 
across all programme villages. 80% of households 
consistently segregate waste and 96% view cleanliness 
as a shared community responsibility. 79% of Paryavaran 
Sakhis have been engaged for over two years, indicating 
strong frontline retention. The majority of Sakhis earn 
above ` 6,000 per month with universal adoption of 
savings behaviour. The programme has demonstrated 
a scalable, community-owned, women-led model for 
sustainable solid waste management.
	
Impact Assessment 6:
	
Project: Local Area Development / Healthcare
	
CSR initiative: Stem Cell Laboratory & Hospital 
Infrastructure — Dr. Shroff's Charity Eye Hospital, Delhi
	
Impact assessment carried out by: PHFI Institute 
of Public Health Sciences, Hyderabad (Deemed to be 
University)
	
The Company provided two grants to Dr. Shroff's 
Charity Eye Hospital (SCEH), Delhi — a three-year 
grant to establish the Eicher-Shroff Centre for 
Ocular Regeneration (Centre for Regeneration and 
Translational Medicine, CRTM) and a one-year grant 
for hospital infrastructure upgradation. The evaluation 
was conducted by PHFI-IIPHH with fieldwork in 
February 2026.
	
Grant 1 — Stem Cell Laboratory (CRTM)
	
Findings — The CRTM (Center for Regeneration and 
Translational Medicine) is a fully operational BSL-2 
certified stem cell research facility — the first of its 
kind in a charitable eye hospital in North India. Within 
the grant period, the laboratory produced six peer-
reviewed publications in national and international 
ophthalmology journals, 18 poster presentations and 
three oral presentations at conferences including ARVO 
(Association for Research in Vision and Ophthalmology). 
Five patents have been filed and two research products 
are progressing through the CDSCO (Central Drugs 
Standard Control Organization) regulatory pipeline 
towards clinical trials. A PhD programme was initiated 
with Manipal Academy of Higher Education (MAHE), 
enrolling five PhD scholars. National and international 
collaborations were established with 9 international 
universities (including University of Missouri, University 
College London, and Kyoto University), seven national 
institutions, and eight industry partners. Out of the 
25-30 external grant proposals submitted, 8-10 were 
successfully awarded including grants from ICMR (Indian 
Council of Medical Research), DBT (Department of 
Biotechnology), and DRDO (Defence Research and 
Development Organization).
	
Grant 2 — Hospital Infrastructure Upgradation
	
Findings — The infrastructure grant resulted in the 
construction of 12 new clinical rooms including OPD 
examination rooms, counsellor rooms, phlebotomy 
rooms, and accessible toilets, all fully functional. 
Patient footfall increased from approximately 500 to 
1,200 patients per day. Average waiting time halved 
from 20 to 10 minutes. The vision centre outreach 
network expanded from 14 to 114 centres, with 60-
70% of patients now referred through these centres.
